source_text:
Fragmentum in epistulam ad Philemonem (in catenis)
Phm
1,1 Ἐν πολλαῖς ἐπιστολαῖς ξένον τίθησι ῥῆμα τοῦ μέλλοντος εἰσάγεσθαι λόγου
κατασκευαστικόν, καὶ νῦν ἐπειδὴ ἔμελλεν ἀξιοῦν ὑπὲρ Ὀνησίμου τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ἀξίᾳ–
ἀξία δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸ δεδέσθαι–, τὸ ἀξιόπιστον τῆς παρακλήσεως δείκνυσιν.
thought_title: Paul's imprisonment as the ground of his appeal's credibility
orientation: Oecumenius is explaining Philemon 1:1, where Paul's mention of his imprisonment prepares for his request on behalf of Onesimus.
pass_a_gloss: In many letters he places an unusual word that prepares for the argument about to be introduced, and now since he was about to make an appeal on behalf of Onesimus by his own worth—and his worth is his imprisonment—, he shows the credibility of the appeal.

choices.why: Literal rendering of ξένον as 'strange' preserves the sense of an unusual or unexpected word Paul inserts.
Renders the adjective as a relative clause to keep the literal force of the word as preparing or equipping for the coming argument.
The verb means to deem worthy or ask; here it is Paul's request on behalf of Onesimus, so 'make a request' is literal and clear.
Dative of means; 'by his own worth' keeps the instrumental force and the glossary term 'worth'.
The perfect passive infinitive is rendered as a noun phrase per the glossary, avoiding banned renderings like 'being bound' or 'being in chains'.
Both terms follow the glossary; 'credibility' for ἀξιόπιστον and 'appeal' for παρακλήσεως.

bible_refs.note: The fragment comments on Philemon 1:1, where Paul mentions his imprisonment.

pass_b_english: In many letters Paul places a strange word that prepares for the argument he is about to introduce. Here too, since he was about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus, he shows the credibility of the appeal by his own worth—and his worth is the imprisonment.

problems.why: Same Greek term rendered two ways; reader may think different concepts.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'unusual word' or 'strange word' throughout.

problems.why: Same action described with different verbs; 'request' vs 'appeal'.
Definite article vs possessive changes emphasis; reader may miss Paul's ownership.
Same Greek term rendered two ways across parallel sections; reader may think different words are meant.
problems.fix: Standardize to one English rendering across all sections.

problems.why: 'Request' and 'appeal' alternate for the same concept; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently across all parallel sections.

problems.why: Definite article vs. possessive pronoun before 'imprisonment' across parallel sections.
problems.fix: Standardize to one phrasing across all sections.

fixed: Standardized 'strange word' to 'unusual word' in both English and gloss.
Standardized 'make a request' to 'make an appeal' in both English and gloss.
Standardized 'the imprisonment' to 'his imprisonment' in both English and gloss.
